blocks.content:
Article 214 states that there shall be a High Court for each state.

Key Points:
• Parliament can establish a common High Court.
• Example: Punjab and Haryana share a common High Court.
Article 214 states that there shall be a High Court for each state.

rows: Article 214 mandates a High Court for each individual state
Parliament can establish a shared High Court for multiple states

items: Article 214 is frequently tested in questions regarding the constitutional basis of State High Courts.
Exams often ask which authority can establish a common High Court—the correct answer is Parliament.
Punjab and Haryana are commonly cited in exam questions as an example of states sharing a common High Court.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 214 provides the constitutional mandate that there shall be a High Court for each state.
The Indian Parliament holds the legal authority to establish a common High Court for two or more states.
Punjab and Haryana serve as a primary example of states sharing a single common High Court.
